item.title: Young woman seriously injured in single-vehicle accident on Route 463 in Binyamin
item.description:
A 22-year-old woman was seriously injured in a single-vehicle accident after the car she was traveling in struck a guardrail on Route 463 in the Binyamin region.
Magen David Adom (MDA) paramedics evacuated her by helicopter to Sheba Hospital at Tel Hashomer. The driver sustained minor injuries. Police have launched an investigation.

item.title: Central Elections Committee publishes final election results
item.description:
Central Elections Committee Publishes Final Election Results
The Central Elections Committee has published the final results of Israel's 26th Knesset elections following the completion of the double-envelope ballot count and an initial review of the results from regular polling stations.
According to the results, Likud won 27 seats, Yashar 21, Beyachad 12, and the Joint List 11. The Democrats and Ra'am each won eight seats, while Yisrael Beytenu, Otzma Yehudit, and United Torah Judaism secured seven seats each. Shas and the Religious Zionist Party each won six seats. All other parties failed to cross the electoral threshold. The current coalition secured 53 seats, the change bloc 48, and the Arab parties a combined 19.
Voter turnout stood at 77.9%. A total of 5,716,665 votes were counted, of which 5,690,778 were valid and 25,887 were invalid. The electoral threshold was 3.25%, equivalent to 184,947 votes.
The Central Elections Committee clarified that the results remain subject to election integrity checks and minor adjustments that may be made during the verification process. The results will be submitted to the President of Israel on Wednesday, November 4.

item.title: Eisenkot: I will not allow any delay to swearing in of Knesset
item.description:
Yashar party chairman Gadi Eisenkot accused Likud and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of conducting a "coordinated and organized campaign to delegitimize the election results," stressing that he would not allow any delay in the swearing-in of the Knesset.
Eisenkot announced that his teams were preparing to submit bills when the Knesset convenes, adding: "The days when Netanyahu used the institutions of government against Israel's interests and for his own personal needs are over."
